newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nissan to raise S.Africa output by Automakers deal.
newsitem.headline: Nissan to raise S.Africa output by Automakers deal.

text.p: Nissan Motor Co Ltd said on Friday it aims to boost output and sales in South Africa by buying a 50 percent stake in South African car maker Automakers Ltd.

"Nissan intends to further solidify the foundations of its manufacturing and sales activities in the South African market that is projected to continue growing into the future," the company said in a statement.
Earlier, Automakers announced that a pact had been finalised between its majority shareholder Sankorp and Nissan for Nissan to acquire 50 percent of Automakers.

Sankorp will sell 92.5 million shares in Automakers, representing half the equity, to Nissan with effect from July 1. Nissan is to pay 360.75 million rand for the stake, or 390 cents per ordinary share.
Nissan said it had been expanding exports throughout Africa except the North African region by making its South African base the hub of export trade.
By becoming the largest shareholder in Automakers, Nissan said it plans to further reinforce its export business from South Africa.

The decision followed a similar move by its rival Toyota Motor Corp, which in last October bought a 27.8 percent stake in Toyota South Africa Ltd (TSA) for 446 million rand to boost its global competitiveness. TSA is 50 percent owned by Wesco, an independent South African holding company.
Car sales in South Africa rose to 365,000 units in 1995 from 300,000 in 1994, industry sources said.
